newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 21.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 21. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Indonesia should aim for an inflation rate of below five percent by the end of the sixth five-year development plan in 1999, economists said.
Transmigration Minister Siswono Yudohusodo said Indonesia hopes to move around 80,000 people from the overpopulated island of Java to some of the archipelago's more outlying islands in 1997/8.
President Suharto said that wealth created by the country's development should be spread throughout Indonesian society and not just amongst a few rich conglomerates.

Bishop Carlos Belo has asked the German magazine Der Spiegel to apologise to the Indonesian government and armed forces for distorting his words in a recent interview. Belo reportedly said Indonesia treated Timorese like "scabby dogs", a comment which the bishop denied ever making.
